A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVTRv2 research and contain readable main text and supplementary Sections 6–12. Their equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition experiments, component ablations, dataset-overlap analysis, timing measurements, and recognition-error analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds comparator results and an experiment using synthetic pretraining followed by real-data fine-tuning.

M1.justification: The MSR resizing rules, visual backbone, FRM and SGM operations, optimization losses, and Tiny/Small/Base architectures remain unchanged. Additional architectural explanations and the new pretraining evaluation do not establish a revised recognition algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 uses the Real dataset for fine-tuning in the new Table 6 experiment; v1 discussed it through overlap analysis rather than using it to train SVTRv2. Com, U14M, OST, LTB, BCTR, and the synthetic ST+MJ datasets were already covered.

E2.justification: v2 adds IGTR-AR and SMTR to the real-trained and synthetic-trained comparisons, and DPTR, IGTR-AR, and SMTR to the Chinese comparison. New Table 6 compares against E2STR, VL-Reader, CLIP4STR, DPTR, and IGTR, substantially extending comparison coverage to pretrained recognizers.

E3.justification: Table 6 introduces synthetic pretraining followed by Real-dataset fine-tuning and evaluation on Com and OST. The existing experiments retain their stated splits, metrics, length restrictions, training budgets, and timing procedure. Expanded tuning descriptions do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 12 adds a brief tuning-effect analysis, reporting gains over default configurations and a MAERec example of 78.6% versus 85.2%. Existing component ablations, backbone-transfer checks, overlap analysis, and failure-case analyses retain their evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain point-estimate reporting; the added hyperparameter-tuning discussion does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing shared comparison rows retain their numerical values, but added results materially change rankings. Section 4.3 changes SVTRv2-B's leading-scenario count from 12/15 to 9/15; added SMTR scores 55.5 on LTB versus SVTRv2-B's 50.2. Synthetic-data IGTR-AR scores 65.07 on U14M versus SVTRv2's retained 62.83. New Table 6 reports SVTRv2-B at 97.83 on Com and 86.9 on OST under the additional training regime, not a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's Equations 3–4 explicitly deriving the combined FRM mapping from horizontal and vertical rearrangement matrices. It retains the overall mapping formulation, attention operations, and losses. This is a limited removal of mathematical derivation rather than merely equation renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows outperforming 'all' EDTRs to 'most' and extends the stated evaluation scope to pretraining. The conclusion also incorporates pretraining performance. The central MSR, FRM, SGM, and filtered-benchmark contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 explains convolutions as supplying positional information without absolute positional encoding and explicitly qualifies the purely CTC architecture as applying during inference. Section 8 limits the Real/REBU-Syn leakage objection to U14M evaluation. Section 10 replaces synthetic-data superiority with competitiveness, while the existing failure-mode limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents absent absolute positional encoding, the FRM MLP expansion factor of four, and model-specific tuning with best-result selection. It removes mixed-precision statements from Section 4.1 and the supplementary settings table. Hardware, code access, architecture specifications, and most training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds ABINet++, PETR, DPTR, CLIP4STR, E2STR, and VL-Reader references and discusses competition with pretrained recognizers; MobileNets and VGG references disappear. CPPD, SMTR, and IGTR were already cited in v1, so their publication updates are not new cited works. The main related-work framing remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are edited, the FRM exposition is shortened and rewritten, and several supplementary passages are polished. MSR terminology and mistaken model names are corrected, the affiliation changes, and an acknowledgement is added. The overall section sequence and much of the exposition are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6, expands existing comparison tables, relocates Figure 3 and supplementary tables, and revises captions and diagram labels. Figure 6 is redrawn and the overlap table is widened. The overall visual format and existing qualitative examples, including Figures 7–8, are retained.

improvement.justification: Broader contemporary comparisons and more restrained abstract and synthetic-data claims make v2's empirical assessment more informative and better grounded. The pretraining comparison adds useful evidence, although changed training data prevent isolating a pretraining benefit. These gains are modest: core results remain unchanged, some blanket superiority wording persists, and the explicit FRM derivation and mixed-precision disclosure are removed.
